# AI usage during the development process

**Current state (since Phase 4, see below): all active development is done with Claude Code.**
Earlier phases used Gemini for the initial design and tooling work, kept below as historical
record — not because it's still in use.

## Early phases (Gemini)

Gemini Pro (personal subscription, via Google One 2T) was used in-browser (Brave / Google Chrome).
Chats were exported as markdown files (not always working perfectly) using the browser extension
`AI Chat Exporter`. Both Fast and Thinking models were used, depending on the need.

1. **Phase 1** — Gaining general knowledge about dashboard development. First architectural design
   thinking.
2. **Phase 2** — Development of a specialized agent for development: see
   [DashBoard_Architect_v1](./DashBoard_Architect_v1.qmd) (February 2026). Used iteratively to
   refine requirements and design understanding, review notes, ask clarifying questions, create
   the basic architectural structure and boilerplate, and design the repository structure so it
   reflects the intended architecture and stays maintainable.
3. **Phase 3** — Full agentic integration (March 2026+): execution and active code development
   were driven by the **Antigravity** framework with full agentic integration with Gemini Pro.
   The agent directly managed workspace standards (ADRs), created test data schemas, refactored
   codebase architecture, and enforced data contracts.

## Current phase: Claude Code

4. **Phase 4** — All active development since (the whole second half of this project's history —
   roughly a third of all commits are Claude-co-authored, and climbing) is done with
   **Claude Code**, replacing the Antigravity/Gemini workflow entirely. The project owner directs
   the work, reviews the agent's plans and findings, and makes every product/scope decision; the
   agent implements, tests and documents within rules the owner has written down:

   - **Rules first.** `CLAUDE.md` plus `.claude/rules/*.md` govern architecture, path authority,
     the UI contract, naming conventions, and how to handle deprecation — read every session, not
     optional guidance.
   - **Decisions are logged, not just made.** Every significant architectural choice becomes a
     dated, numbered entry in `.claude/knowledge/architecture_decisions.md` — the record of *why*,
     not just *what*.
   - **Audits replace ad-hoc review for the mechanical parts.** Scheduled scripts
     (`scripts/audit_*.py`) check dependency health, documentation-vs-code drift,
     task-vs-code drift, config consistency and UML-model-vs-code consistency — the things a human
     reviewer would otherwise have to re-derive from scratch every time. Findings are triaged
     (fixed or explicitly accepted) rather than left to accumulate silently.
   - **Every fix gets a test, and the test gets tested.** New regression tests are
     mutation-tested: the fix is temporarily reverted to confirm the new test actually fails
     without it, then restored — a test that could never have caught the bug isn't mistaken for
     real coverage.
   - **Real bugs become GitHub issues**, filed before or alongside the fix and closed with the
     evidence once resolved, so there is a trace — not just a silently-fixed local note.
   - **What AI-assisted does *not* yet mean here: human-code-reviewed.** See the notice at the top
     of the project [README](../../README.md) — no one has yet manually read and verified the
     generated source line by line. That review is planned, one module at a time, before any
     deployment handling real data.
